identity.real_world_identity_notes: PMR identifies the Historic USV8 entry as the 1970 Plymouth Barracuda. Exact-model AAR Barracuda references support a four-speed manual H-pattern baseline; race-specific gearbox construction, technique, and wheel hardware remain open.

wheel_rim.notes: Exact real-car wheel details were not established by the reviewed sources.

The exact-model museum reference documents a four-speed manual; exact race-car applicability remains a review gap. The documented four-speed manual supports an H-pattern baseline. No exact race gate image establishes a dogleg, so the conventional period layout is retained as a low-confidence baseline. An H-pattern manual requires clutch use to move off from rest under the project derivation rule. driver_summary: AAR stood for Dan Gurney's All American Racers: Plymouth built about 2,700 AAR 'Cudas to homologate the Barracuda for 1970 Trans-Am, where Gurney and Swede Savage raced it for one season.
